items.content: Author/Poet: Vikram Seth. Important keywords: satire, foolish governance, king, justice, irony, absurdity, democracy, public opinion, authority, corruption, humour.

items.title: Present Simple
items.front: Subject + V1(s/es) + Object
items.back: Used for habits, routines, general truths and repeated actions. Example: She studies every evening.

items.title: Present Continuous
items.front: Subject + am/is/are + V-ing + Object
items.back: Used for an action happening now or around the present time. Example: They are preparing for the test.

items.title: Present Perfect
items.front: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
items.back: Used for completed actions connected with the present. Example: I have finished my homework.

items.title: Present Perfect Continuous
items.front: Subject + has/have been + V-ing + Object
items.back: Used for an action that began in the past and continues up to the present. Example: He has been studying for two hours.

items.title: Past Simple
items.front: Subject + V2 + Object
items.back: Used for a completed action in the past. Example: We visited the museum yesterday.

items.title: Past Continuous
items.front: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object
items.back: Used for an action that was in progress at a particular time in the past. Example: She was reading at 8 p.m.

items.title: Past Perfect
items.front: Subject + had + V3 + Object
items.back: Used for an action completed before another past action. Example: The train had left before we arrived.

items.title: Past Perfect Continuous
items.front: Subject + had been + V-ing + Object
items.back: Used for an action continuing for a period before another past event. Example: They had been waiting for an hour before the bus came.

items.title: Future Simple
items.front: Subject + will + V1 + Object
items.back: Used for predictions, promises, decisions and future actions. Example: I will call you tomorrow.

items.title: Future Continuous
items.front: Subject + will be + V-ing + Object
items.back: Used for an action that will be in progress at a particular future time. Example: This time tomorrow, I will be travelling.

items.title: Future Perfect
items.front: Subject + will have + V3 + Object
items.back: Used for an action that will be completed before a specified future time. Example: She will have finished the project by Friday.

items.title: Future Perfect Continuous
items.formula: Subject + will have been + V-ing + Object
items.front: Subject + will have been + V-ing + Object
items.back: Used for an action continuing up to a particular future point. Example: By June, he will have been working here for a year.

items.title: Noun Clause
items.front: A clause that functions as a noun in a sentence.
items.back: Example: I know what you mean. The clause “what you mean” acts as the object of “know”.

items.title: Adjective Clause
items.front: A clause that describes or qualifies a noun or pronoun.
items.back: Example: The student who won the prize is my friend. The clause “who won the prize” describes the student.

items.title: Adverb Clause
items.front: A clause that functions like an adverb and tells when, why, how, where or under what condition an action occurs.
items.back: Example: We stayed inside because it was raining. The clause gives the reason for staying inside.

items.title: Simile
items.front: A comparison between two unlike things using “like” or “as”.
items.back: Example: The moon shone like a silver lamp.

items.title: Metaphor
items.front: A direct comparison in which one thing is described as another.
items.back: Example: The classroom was a beehive of activity.

items.title: Personification
items.front: Giving human qualities or actions to non-human things.
items.back: Example: The wind whispered through the trees.

items.title: Alliteration
items.front: Repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words.
items.back: Example: Silent seas softly shimmered.

items.title: Assonance
items.front: Repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words.
items.back: Example: The rain stayed late in the grey day.

items.title: Consonance
items.front: Repetition of consonant sounds within or at the ends of nearby words.
items.back: Example: The lumpy, bumpy road shook the car.

items.title: Onomatopoeia
items.front: A word whose sound imitates the sound it describes.
items.back: Example: The bees buzzed around the flowers.

items.title: Imagery
items.front: Descriptive language that creates a vivid sensory picture in the reader’s mind.
items.back: Example: Warm bread, fresh butter and cinnamon filled the kitchen with a rich smell.

items.title: Repetition
items.front: Deliberate repetition of a word, phrase or idea for emphasis.
items.back: Example: Never give up, never lose hope.

items.title: Refrain
items.front: A line or group of lines repeated at intervals in a poem or song.
items.back: Example: A repeated closing line returns after each stanza.

items.title: Enjambment
items.front: Continuation of a sentence or thought from one poetic line to the next without a terminal pause.
items.back: Example: The river moved beyond the hill / and disappeared into the mist.

items.title: Rhyme
items.front: Similarity of sound, especially at the ends of lines.
items.back: Example: The words “light” and “night” rhyme.

items.title: Rhyme Scheme
items.front: The pattern of end rhymes in a poem, usually represented with letters.
items.back: Example: A poem with alternating end sounds may follow an ABAB scheme.

items.title: Oxymoron
items.front: A combination of words with apparently contradictory meanings.
items.back: Example: The room was filled with deafening silence.

items.title: Hyperbole
items.front: Deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis or effect.
items.back: Example: I have told you a million times.

items.title: Irony
items.front: A contrast between what is expected and what actually happens, or between literal and intended meaning.
items.back: Example: A fire station catches fire.

items.title: Symbolism
items.front: Using an object, action or image to represent a deeper idea.
items.back: Example: A rising sun can symbolize hope or a new beginning.

items.title: Apostrophe
items.front: Directly addressing an absent person, an abstract idea or a non-human thing.
items.back: Example: O Time, why do you move so quickly?

items.title: Paradox
items.front: A statement that appears contradictory but can express a meaningful truth.
items.back: Example: Less is more.

items.title: Antithesis
items.front: Placing contrasting ideas close together for emphasis.
items.back: Example: Many speak, but few listen.

chapters.name: Changing Trends & Career in Physical Education

items.title: Physical Education
items.content: Physical Education is an educational process that uses physical activities to develop physical fitness, motor abilities, knowledge, attitudes and desirable behaviour.

items.title: Aims of Physical Education
items.content: Major aims include physical development, mental development, social development, emotional development and development of healthy habits and desirable values through physical activity.
items.keywords: aims objectives physical mental social emotional development

items.title: Changing Trends in Sports
items.content: The syllabus covers changes in playing surfaces, wearable gear, sports equipment and technological advancements in sports.
items.keywords: sports trends playing surface wearable gear equipment technology

items.title: Career Areas in Physical Education
items.content: Career opportunities include teaching, coaching, sports management and other professional roles connected with physical education and sports.
items.keywords: career physical education teacher coach sports manager

items.title: Khelo India
items.content: Khelo India is a national sports development initiative covered in the Class XI Physical Education syllabus.

items.title: Fit India Movement
items.content: Fit India promotes fitness as part of everyday life and encourages people to adopt physically active lifestyles.
items.keywords: Fit India fitness movement active lifestyle

items.title: Olympism
items.content: Olympism combines sport with educational and cultural values and promotes a way of life based on effort, respect and ethical conduct.
items.keywords: Olympism Olympic values sport education culture

items.title: Excellence
items.content: Excellence means striving to do one's best and continuously improve through effort and commitment.

items.title: Friendship
items.content: Friendship represents understanding, solidarity and mutual respect among people through sport.

items.title: Respect
items.content: Respect includes respect for oneself, others, rules, fair play and the environment of sport.
items.keywords: Olympic value respect fair play rules

items.title: Fair Play
items.content: Fair play means following rules, respecting opponents and officials, and competing honestly without gaining an unfair advantage.

items.title: Olympic Symbol
items.content: The Olympic symbol consists of five interlocking rings representing the union of the five continents associated with the Olympic movement.

items.title: Olympic Motto
items.content: The Olympic motto expresses the idea of striving higher, faster and stronger, with the modern form also emphasizing togetherness.
items.keywords: Olympic motto faster higher stronger together

items.title: Sports Ethics
items.content: Sports ethics concerns honest participation, respect, fair play, responsibility and rejection of cheating or unethical conduct.

items.title: Yoga
items.content: Yoga is a discipline involving practices that support integration of body, mind and behaviour.

items.title: Aim of Yoga
items.content: Yoga practices in physical education are associated with physical fitness, mental well-being, concentration, discipline and balanced development.

items.title: Asana
items.content: An asana is a yogic posture practiced with controlled body positioning and stability.

items.title: Pranayama
items.content: Pranayama refers to yogic practices involving regulation and control of breathing.

items.title: Dhyana
items.content: Dhyana refers to meditation or sustained concentration of the mind.

items.title: General Benefits of Yoga
items.content: Yoga practices may support flexibility, balance, posture, concentration, relaxation and general physical and mental well-being.
items.keywords: yoga benefits flexibility balance posture concentration

items.title: CWSN
items.content: CWSN refers to Children With Special Needs. Physical education should provide appropriate opportunities for participation while considering individual abilities and needs.
items.keywords: CWSN children special needs physical education

items.title: Adapted Physical Education
items.content: Adapted physical education modifies activities, equipment, rules or teaching methods when necessary so students with different abilities can participate meaningfully.

items.title: Inclusion in Physical Education
items.content: Inclusive physical education aims to provide equitable participation and learning opportunities for students with different abilities.

items.title: Types of Disability
items.content: The chapter addresses disability-related participation and the need to understand individual limitations and capabilities when planning physical activities.

items.title: Adapting an Activity
items.content: When adapting an activity, consider the student's ability, safety, equipment, space, rules, instructions and the level of assistance required.
items.keywords: adapt activity CWSN safety equipment rules

items.title: Physical Fitness
items.content: Physical fitness is the ability to perform daily activities effectively, efficiently and without undue fatigue, while retaining enough energy for leisure and unexpected demands.

items.title: Wellness
items.content: Wellness is a multidimensional state associated with balanced physical, mental, emotional and social functioning and healthy lifestyle choices.

items.title: Health and Fitness
items.content: Health is broader than physical fitness. Fitness is one component that contributes to overall health and well-being.

items.title: Health-Related Fitness Components
items.content: Important health-related components include cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition.

items.title: Skill-Related Fitness Components
items.content: Skill-related fitness commonly includes speed, agility, balance, coordination, power and reaction ability.
items.keywords: skill related fitness speed agility balance coordination power reaction

items.title: Healthy Lifestyle Factors
items.content: Regular physical activity, balanced nutrition, adequate rest, hygiene, stress management and avoidance of harmful habits contribute to a healthy lifestyle.
items.keywords: healthy lifestyle exercise nutrition rest hygiene

items.title: Test
items.content: A test is a tool or procedure used to obtain information about a person's knowledge, physical ability, skill or other characteristic.

items.title: Measurement
items.content: Measurement is the numerical or graded data obtained from an applied test. It may be quantitative, qualitative, or both.

items.title: Evaluation
items.content: Evaluation is the process of interpreting collected data and making a professional judgement about its value or worth.

items.title: Push-up Test
items.content: Measures upper-limb muscular strength and muscular endurance. Score = maximum number of correctly performed push-ups completed according to the specified rate or time.
items.keywords: push up muscular strength endurance score

items.title: Abdominal Curl Test
items.content: Assesses muscular strength and endurance of the abdominal muscles. Score is the number of correctly completed curl-ups in the specified time or at the specified rate.

items.title: Squat Thrust Test
items.content: Assesses muscular strength and endurance of the lower body. Score = maximum number of successive squat thrusts performed in 1 minute.
items.keywords: squat thrust lower body strength endurance

items.title: 1000 Metre Run/Walk Test
items.content: Used to assess cardiovascular endurance. The participant covers 1000 m in the shortest possible time; walking is allowed. Score = recorded time in minutes and seconds.
items.keywords: 1000 metre run walk cardiovascular endurance time

items.title: Sit-and-Reach Test
items.content: Measures flexibility of the lower back and hamstring muscle group. The score is recorded in centimetres.
items.keywords: sit and reach flexibility hamstring lower back

items.title: Sit-and-Reach Difference Ratings
items.content: NCERT reference values for the difference between measurements: Poor = 15 cm; Fair = 25 cm; Good = 30 cm; Very Good = 35 cm; Excellent = 40 cm.
items.keywords: sit reach poor fair good very good excellent centimetre

items.title: Body Mass Index (BMI)
items.symbols: Weight in kilograms; height in metres
items.explanation: BMI is calculated by dividing body weight by the square of height.
items.keywords: BMI body mass index weight height obesity

items.title: BMI Interpretation for Ages 2–20
items.content: NCERT states that BMI is calculated using the same formula for children aged 2–20, but the adult-style BMI ranges should not be used for judgement. The result is compared with a percentile table for the same sex and age: below the 5th percentile = underweight; 5th–85th = normal; 85th–95th = overweight; above 95th = obese.
items.keywords: BMI children adolescents percentile 2 20 underweight normal overweight obese

items.title: BMI Table Given in NCERT
items.content: NCERT lists these general reference categories: very severely underweight below 15; severely underweight 15–16; underweight 16–18.5; normal/healthy weight 18.5–24; overweight 25–29.9; obesity 30 and above. For ages 2–20, use age- and sex-specific percentiles instead of these ranges.

items.title: Waist-to-Hip Ratio (WHR)
items.symbols: W = waist circumference; H = hip circumference
items.explanation: Both measurements should be taken using the same unit, so the units cancel in the ratio.
items.keywords: WHR waist hip ratio body fat distribution

items.title: WHR Worked Example
items.content: Example from the NCERT chapter: waist = 76 cm and hip = 97 cm.

items.title: WHR Risk-Level Reference
items.content: NCERT gives the following reference values: Men ≤0.95 and women ≤0.80 = low risk; men 0.96–1.0 and women 0.81–0.85 = moderate risk; men ≥1.0 and women ≥0.85 = high risk.
items.keywords: WHR norms low moderate high risk men women

items.title: Basic Body Measurements
items.content: Body weight is recorded in kilograms using a weighing machine. Height is measured using an anthropometer or stadiometer and recorded in centimetres. For BMI, height must be converted to metres before applying the formula.
items.keywords: height weight anthropometer stadiometer kilograms centimetres BMI

items.title: Waist and Hip Measurement
items.content: For waist measurement, stand straight and breathe out; place the tape around the waist just above the belly button. For hip measurement, place the tape around the widest part of the hip. Record both measurements consistently.
items.keywords: waist measurement hip measurement WHR procedure

items.title: Muscular Strength
items.content: The ability of a muscle or group of muscles to overcome or act against resistance. NCERT lists push-ups, abdominal curls and squat thrust as tests related to muscular strength.
items.keywords: muscular strength push up abdominal curl squat thrust

items.title: Muscular Endurance
items.content: The ability of muscles to perform muscular activity over a period of time, or the duration for which muscular strength can be applied. NCERT associates the 1000 metre run/walk test with cardiovascular endurance.
items.keywords: muscular endurance cardiovascular endurance stamina 1000 metre

items.title: Somatotypes
items.content: NCERT describes three somatotypes: Endomorph, Mesomorph and Ectomorph. The chapter presents them as body-type classifications with different physical characteristics.
items.keywords: endomorph mesomorph ectomorph somatotype body type

items.title: Skin Fold Measurement — 3-Site
items.content: A 3-site skinfold measurement is an anthropometric method used to assess subcutaneous fat. The CBSE Class XI 2026–27 syllabus specifically includes 3-site skinfold measurement under Test, Measurement & Evaluation.
items.keywords: skin fold skinfold 3-site anthropometric body composition measurement

chapters.name: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology in Sports

items.title: Anatomy
items.content: Anatomy is the study of the structure of the human body and its parts.

items.title: Physiology
items.content: Physiology is the study of how the body and its organs function.

items.title: Skeletal System
items.content: The skeletal system provides support, protects internal organs, enables movement with muscles and provides sites for muscle attachment.
items.keywords: skeletal system bones support protection movement

items.title: Axial Skeleton
items.content: The axial skeleton forms the central framework of the body and includes the skull, vertebral column and thoracic cage.
items.keywords: axial skeleton skull vertebral column thoracic cage

items.title: Appendicular Skeleton
items.content: The appendicular skeleton includes the bones of the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.
items.keywords: appendicular skeleton limbs pectoral pelvic girdle

items.title: Joint
items.content: A joint is the junction or connection between two or more bones.

items.title: Types of Joints
items.content: Important joint classifications include fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial joints. Synovial joints allow substantial movement and include hinge, ball-and-socket and pivot examples.
items.keywords: joints fibrous cartilaginous synovial hinge ball socket pivot

items.title: Types of Muscles
items.content: The three major muscle types are skeletal muscle, smooth muscle and cardiac muscle. Skeletal muscle is primarily associated with voluntary body movement.

items.title: Cardiovascular System
items.content: The cardiovascular system consists primarily of the heart, blood and blood vessels and transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones and metabolic wastes.

items.title: Heart Chambers
items.content: The human heart has four chambers: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium and left ventricle.

items.title: Blood Vessels
items.content: Arteries generally carry blood away from the heart, veins generally carry blood toward the heart, and capillaries permit exchange between blood and tissues.

items.title: Respiratory System
items.content: The respiratory system enables ventilation and gas exchange, supplying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.
items.keywords: respiratory system ventilation gas exchange oxygen carbon dioxide

items.title: Inspiration
items.content: During normal inspiration, the diaphragm contracts and moves downward while the thoracic cavity expands, allowing air to enter the lungs.

items.title: Expiration
items.content: During normal expiration, the diaphragm relaxes and the thoracic cavity decreases in volume, helping air leave the lungs.

items.title: Exercise and Heart Rate
items.content: During physical activity, heart rate generally increases so that cardiac output can support the greater demand of working tissues.

items.title: Exercise and Respiration
items.content: During exercise, ventilation increases to improve oxygen delivery and carbon-dioxide removal according to the body's increased metabolic demand.
items.keywords: exercise respiration ventilation oxygen carbon dioxide

chapters.name: Fundamentals of Kinesiology and Biomechanics in Sports

items.title: Kinesiology
items.content: Kinesiology is the study of human movement.

items.title: Biomechanics
items.content: Biomechanics applies mechanical principles to the study of human movement and sports performance.

items.title: Kinematics
items.content: Kinematics describes motion using quantities such as position, displacement, velocity and acceleration without focusing on the forces causing the motion.

items.title: Kinetics
items.content: Kinetics studies the forces and torques associated with movement.

items.title: Force
items.symbols: F = force; m = mass; a = acceleration
items.explanation: Force is related to mass and acceleration.

items.title: Linear Momentum
items.symbols: p = momentum; m = mass; v = velocity

items.title: Torque
items.content: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis or pivot. It depends on the magnitude of force and its perpendicular distance from the axis.

items.title: Balance
items.content: Balance is the ability to maintain or control the body's position. It may be static or dynamic.

items.title: Equilibrium
items.content: Equilibrium is a state in which the net effect of forces and moments is balanced so that the body remains at rest or continues in uniform motion.

items.title: Levers in the Human Body
items.content: A lever consists of a rigid structure, an axis or fulcrum, an effort and a resistance. The human body uses bones and joints as components of lever systems during movement.
items.keywords: lever fulcrum effort resistance bones joints

items.title: Planes of Movement
items.content: The major anatomical planes used to describe movement are sagittal, frontal and transverse planes.

items.title: Axes of Movement
items.content: The major axes used to describe body movement are longitudinal, transverse and anteroposterior axes.

items.title: Newton's Laws in Sports
items.content: Newton's first law describes inertia; the second relates force, mass and acceleration; the third describes equal and opposite interaction forces.
items.keywords: Newton laws inertia force acceleration action reaction sports

items.title: Growth
items.content: Growth refers mainly to quantitative physical changes such as increases in body size or dimensions.

items.title: Development
items.content: Development refers to progressive qualitative and quantitative changes in physical, mental, emotional and social abilities.

items.title: Adolescence
items.content: Adolescence is a developmental period involving substantial physical, psychological, emotional and social changes between childhood and adulthood.

items.title: Personality
items.content: Personality is the relatively organized pattern of thoughts, feelings and behaviours that characterizes an individual.

items.title: Motivation
items.content: Motivation is the process or set of factors that initiates, directs and sustains behaviour toward a goal.

items.title: Intrinsic Motivation
items.content: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest, enjoyment, satisfaction or personal mastery associated with the activity itself.

items.title: Extrinsic Motivation
items.content: Extrinsic motivation is influenced by external rewards, recognition, competition, approval or other outside consequences.

items.title: Attention
items.content: Attention is the selective focusing of mental resources on relevant information or activity.

items.title: Aggression in Sports
items.content: Aggression refers to behaviour intended to harm or injure another person; sporting contexts require control of aggressive impulses within rules and ethical boundaries.

items.title: Anxiety
items.content: Anxiety is a state involving apprehension or worry that may influence sporting performance. Appropriate preparation and psychological skills can help athletes manage performance-related anxiety.

items.title: Stress
items.content: Stress is a psychological and physiological response to perceived demands or challenges. In sport, its effect depends on the individual and situation.

items.title: Team Cohesion
items.content: Team cohesion is the tendency of group members to remain united and work together toward shared goals.

items.title: Resilience
items.content: Resilience is the ability to adapt to setbacks, challenges and adversity and continue constructive effort.

items.title: Mental Toughness
items.content: Mental toughness refers to psychological qualities that help a sportsperson remain focused, confident, committed and composed under demanding conditions.

items.title: Sports Training
items.content: Sports training is a planned and systematic process designed to improve physical fitness, motor abilities, skills and performance.

items.title: Overload Principle
items.content: Training stimulus must be sufficiently greater than the usual level of demand to produce adaptation, while remaining appropriate and safe.

items.title: Progression Principle
items.content: Training demands should be increased gradually as the body adapts rather than being increased abruptly.

items.title: Specificity Principle
items.content: Training adaptations are specific to the muscles, energy systems, movement patterns and skills being trained.

items.title: Reversibility Principle
items.content: Training adaptations can decrease when training is substantially reduced or stopped for a prolonged period.

items.title: Training Adaptation
items.content: Adaptation is the body's response to repeated training stress that enables it to cope more effectively with the same or greater demands.

items.title: Recovery
items.content: Recovery is the period and process through which the body restores and adapts after training. Adequate rest, nutrition and hydration support recovery.

items.title: Warm-up
items.content: Warm-up prepares the body and mind for activity through progressive physical activity and mobility work and can improve readiness for performance.

items.title: Cool-down / Limbering Down
items.content: Cool-down gradually reduces activity after exercise and supports a controlled transition toward the resting state.

items.title: Skill
items.content: A skill is an acquired ability to perform a movement or task effectively and efficiently.

items.title: Technique
items.content: Technique is the specific method or movement pattern used to execute a sporting skill.

items.title: Tactics
items.content: Tactics are short-term decisions or actions used during competition to deal with a particular situation or opponent.

items.title: Strategy
items.content: Strategy is a broader plan developed to achieve a competitive objective, often covering the overall approach to a contest.

items.title: Doping
items.content: Doping refers to the use of prohibited substances or methods in sport to gain an unfair performance advantage or otherwise violate anti-doping rules.

items.title: Why Doping Is Prohibited
items.content: Doping can undermine fair competition and may expose athletes to serious health risks. Anti-doping systems therefore prohibit specified substances and methods.
items.keywords: doping prohibited fair play health risks

items.title: Anti-Doping Awareness
items.content: Athletes are responsible for understanding applicable anti-doping rules and seeking qualified medical or anti-doping guidance before using medicines or supplements that could create a rules issue.

items.title: Computer
items.content: An electronic programmable machine that accepts data, processes it according to instructions, stores data and produces output.

items.title: CPU
items.content: The Central Processing Unit executes instructions and controls major processing operations.

items.title: ALU
items.content: The Arithmetic Logic Unit performs arithmetic and logical operations.

items.title: Control Unit
items.content: The Control Unit coordinates instruction execution and movement of data between computer components.

items.title: RAM
items.content: Random Access Memory is volatile primary memory used for programs and data currently being processed.

items.title: ROM
items.content: Read Only Memory is non-volatile memory that retains stored information when power is removed.

items.title: Cache Memory
items.content: High-speed memory used to reduce the average time needed by the CPU to access frequently used data and instructions.

items.title: Secondary Storage
items.content: Non-volatile storage for programs and data. Examples include HDDs, SSDs and optical storage.

items.title: Input Devices
items.content: Devices used to enter data or commands, such as keyboards, mice, scanners and microphones.

items.title: Output Devices
items.content: Devices that present processed information, such as monitors, printers and speakers.

items.title: Bit
items.content: A bit is a basic unit of digital information with a value of 0 or 1.

items.title: Byte
items.content: One byte consists of 8 bits.

items.title: Binary Storage Units
items.content: 1 KiB = 1024 bytes; 1 MiB = 1024 KiB; 1 GiB = 1024 MiB; 1 TiB = 1024 GiB.

items.title: Software
items.content: A collection of programs and related data that instructs a computer to perform tasks.

items.title: System Software
items.content: Software that manages hardware and provides a platform for application software.

items.title: Application Software
items.content: Software designed to perform tasks for users, such as word processing or image editing.

items.title: Utility Software
items.content: Software used for maintenance, management, security or optimization of a computer system.

items.title: Firmware
items.content: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control for hardware.

items.title: Language Translators
items.content: Assemblers, compilers and interpreters translate programming instructions into forms that can be executed or processed.

items.title: Compiler
items.content: A compiler translates a high-level program into a lower-level or machine-oriented form, generally processing the program as a whole.

items.title: Interpreter
items.content: An interpreter translates and executes program instructions during execution, generally processing them incrementally.

items.title: Operating System
items.content: System software that manages hardware and software resources and provides services to users and applications.

items.title: Process Management
items.content: The operating system manages processes and coordinates program execution.

items.title: Memory Management
items.content: The operating system manages allocation and use of memory among programs and system processes.

items.title: File Management
items.content: The operating system organizes and manages files and directories on storage devices.

items.title: Device Management
items.content: The operating system manages communication between software and hardware devices.

items.title: User Interface
items.content: An operating system provides interfaces such as command-line or graphical interfaces for user interaction.

items.title: OS Security
items.content: Operating systems can provide accounts, permissions and access controls to protect system resources.

items.title: AND Identity
items.content: A AND 1 = A

items.title: OR Identity
items.content: A OR 0 = A

items.title: AND Null Law
items.content: A AND 0 = 0

items.title: OR Null Law
items.content: A OR 1 = 1

items.title: Complement AND
items.content: A AND NOT A = 0

items.title: Complement OR
items.content: A OR NOT A = 1

items.title: Double Complement
items.content: NOT(NOT A) = A

items.title: Commutative AND
items.content: A AND B = B AND A

items.title: Commutative OR
items.content: A OR B = B OR A

items.title: Distributive AND
items.content: A AND (B OR C) = (A AND B) OR (A AND C)

items.title: De Morgan's First Law
items.content: NOT(A AND B) = (NOT A) OR (NOT B)

items.title: De Morgan's Second Law
items.content: NOT(A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B)

items.title: Binary
items.content: Base 2 number system using digits 0 and 1.

items.title: Decimal
items.content: Base 10 number system using digits 0 through 9.

items.title: Octal
items.content: Base 8 number system using digits 0 through 7.

items.title: Hexadecimal
items.content: Base 16 number system using 0–9 and A–F.

items.title: Positional Value
items.symbols: position starts at 0 from the right
items.content: For a number with digits d_n...d_1d_0 in base b, its value is the sum of d_i × b^i.

items.title: Binary → Decimal
items.content: Multiply each binary digit by its corresponding power of 2 and add the results.

items.title: Decimal → Binary
items.content: Repeatedly divide the positive integer by 2 and read the remainders from bottom to top.

items.title: Binary → Octal
items.content: Group binary digits into sets of three from the right and convert each group to an octal digit.

items.title: Octal → Binary
items.content: Replace each octal digit with its 3-bit binary representation.

items.title: Binary → Hexadecimal
items.content: Group binary digits into sets of four from the right and convert each group to a hexadecimal digit.

items.title: Hexadecimal → Binary
items.content: Replace each hexadecimal digit with its 4-bit binary representation.

items.title: Unsigned 8-bit Range
items.content: An unsigned 8-bit value represents integers from 0 through 255.

items.title: Problem Solving
items.content: The systematic process of understanding a problem, designing a solution, implementing it and checking the result.

items.title: Algorithm
items.content: A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps for solving a problem.

items.title: Flowchart
items.content: A graphical representation of an algorithm or process using standardized symbols.

items.title: Pseudocode
items.content: A structured, language-independent description of an algorithm using notation resembling programming statements.

items.title: Input–Process–Output
items.content: A common way to describe computational problems: data enters as input, processing transforms it, and the result is produced as output.

items.title: Problem Decomposition
items.content: Break a complex problem into smaller subproblems that can be solved and tested separately.

items.title: Debugging
items.content: The process of finding and correcting errors in a program.

items.title: Testing
items.content: Testing checks whether a program produces the expected results for selected inputs and conditions.

items.title: Syntax Error
items.content: An error caused by violating the rules of a programming language's syntax.

items.title: Logical Error
items.content: An error where a program runs but produces an incorrect result because the algorithm or logic is wrong.

chapters.name: Familiarization with Basics of Python Programming

items.title: Single-Line Comment
items.content: A # begins a single-line comment in Python.

items.title: print()
items.content: Displays text or values as output.

items.title: input()
items.content: Reads a line of user input and returns it as a string.

items.title: Assignment
items.content: Evaluates the expression and assigns the resulting object to the variable.

items.title: Indentation
items.content: Python uses indentation to define blocks of code. Consistent indentation is required.

items.title: Case Sensitivity
items.content: Python is case-sensitive, so identifiers such as name and Name are different.

items.title: Identifier Rules
items.content: An identifier may contain letters, digits and underscores, cannot begin with a digit and cannot be a Python keyword.

items.title: Keyword
items.content: A reserved word with a predefined meaning in Python that cannot be used as an ordinary identifier.

items.title: Literal
items.content: A literal is a fixed value written directly in source code, such as 10, 3.14, True or 'Hello'.

items.title: Variable
items.content: A variable is a name referring to an object or value used by a program.

items.title: int
items.content: Represents integers without a fractional part.

items.title: float
items.content: Represents floating-point numbers.

items.title: bool
items.content: Represents the Boolean values True and False.

items.title: str
items.content: Represents a sequence of characters.

items.title: None
items.content: Represents the absence of a value.

items.title: type()
items.content: Returns the type of an object.

items.title: int()
items.content: Converts a compatible value to an integer.

items.title: float()
items.content: Converts a compatible value to a floating-point number.

items.title: str()
items.content: Converts a value to its string representation.

items.title: Arithmetic Operators
items.content: + addition; - subtraction; * multiplication; / division; // floor division; % remainder; ** exponentiation.

items.title: Relational Operators
items.content: <, <=, >, >=, == and != compare values and produce Boolean results.

items.title: Logical Operators
items.content: and, or and not combine or invert Boolean conditions.

items.title: Membership Operators
items.content: in and not in test membership in a sequence or collection.

items.title: Identity Operators
items.content: is and is not test whether two references point to the same object.

items.title: Core Operator Precedence
items.content: A useful order is: parentheses → exponentiation → unary operators → multiplication/division/floor division/remainder → addition/subtraction → comparisons → not → and → or.

items.title: Division Operators
items.formula: a / b → division; a // b → floor division; a % b → remainder
items.content: The / operator performs true division and returns a floating-point result; the // operator performs floor division and returns the quotient rounded down.

items.title: Expression
items.content: A combination of literals, variables, operators and function calls that produces a value.

items.title: Statement
items.content: An instruction executed by Python.

items.title: Assignment statement
items.content: variable = expression

items.title: Input statement
items.content: variable = input(prompt)

items.title: input() return type
items.content: input() returns the entered data as a string (str). Convert it when numeric input is required.

items.title: Integer input
items.content: n = int(input("Enter n: "))

items.title: Float input
items.content: x = float(input("Enter x: "))

items.title: Output using print()
items.content: print(value1, value2, ...)

items.title: print() separator
items.content: print(a, b, sep="-") places the specified separator between output values.

items.title: print() end
items.content: print(a, end=" ") changes what is printed after the output instead of using the default newline.

items.title: Formatted output with f-string
items.content: f"Name: {name}, Marks: {marks}"

items.title: Operator evaluation
items.content: Python evaluates operators according to precedence and associativity. Parentheses can make the intended order explicit.

items.title: Division result
items.content: The / operator performs division and produces a floating-point result; // performs floor division.

items.title: Type conversion
items.content: Converting a value from one data type to another, such as int("25") or float("3.5").

items.title: Explicit type conversion
items.content: int(value) | float(value) | str(value) | bool(value)

items.title: Flow of Control
items.content: The order in which statements are executed in a program.

items.title: Three basic control structures
items.content: Sequence, selection and iteration are fundamental structures used to control program execution.

items.title: Sequence
items.content: Statements execute one after another in their written order.

items.title: if statement
items.content: if condition:\n    statement

items.title: if-else statement
if-elif-else statement
Condition result
items.content: A condition used for selection evaluates to True or False.

items.title: Nested if
items.content: An if statement placed inside another if, elif or else block.

items.title: for loop
items.content: for variable in sequence:\n    statement

items.title: while loop
items.content: while condition:\n    statement

items.title: Iteration
items.content: Repeated execution of a block of statements.

items.title: range()
items.content: range(stop) | range(start, stop) | range(start, stop, step)

items.title: range() stop value
items.content: The stop value in range() is excluded from the generated sequence.

items.title: break
items.content: break terminates the nearest enclosing loop immediately.

items.title: continue
items.content: continue skips the remaining statements of the current loop iteration and proceeds to the next iteration.

items.title: pass
items.content: pass is a null statement used when syntactic completeness is required but no action is needed.

items.title: Infinite loop
items.content: A loop that does not reach a terminating condition. A while loop can become infinite if its condition never becomes False.

items.title: Indentation in blocks
items.content: Statements belonging to the same control block must use consistent indentation.

items.title: Nested loop
items.content: A loop placed inside another loop. The inner loop executes as part of the outer loop.

items.title: String
items.content: A sequence of characters enclosed in single quotes, double quotes or triple quotes.

items.title: String literals
items.content: Use single quotes, double quotes or triple quotes to create string literals.

items.title: String indexing
items.content: Positive indexing starts at 0 from the left; negative indexing starts at -1 from the right.

items.title: Character access
items.content: s[index]

items.title: String slicing
items.content: s[start:stop:step] extracts a substring. The stop position is excluded.

items.title: Basic slicing
items.content: s[start:stop]

items.title: Strings are immutable
items.content: Individual characters of an existing string cannot be changed directly.

items.title: String concatenation
items.content: Use + to join strings, for example: "Hello" + " World".

items.title: String repetition
items.content: Use * with an integer to repeat a string, for example: "Hi" * 3.

items.title: String membership
items.content: Use in or not in to test whether a character or substring occurs in a string.

items.title: len() for strings
items.content: len(s) returns the number of characters in string s.

items.title: String case methods
items.content: s.upper() | s.lower() | s.title() | s.capitalize()

items.title: Whitespace methods
items.content: s.strip() | s.lstrip() | s.rstrip()

items.title: Search methods
items.content: s.find(sub) returns the first index of sub, or -1 if it is not found; s.count(sub) counts occurrences.

items.title: Replacement method
items.content: s.replace(old, new) returns a string with occurrences of old replaced by new.

items.title: Split method
items.content: s.split(separator) returns a list of substrings separated using the specified separator.

items.title: Join method
items.content: separator.join(iterable) joins strings using separator between them.

items.title: String comparison
items.content: Strings can be compared using relational operators based on lexicographic ordering.

items.title: Escape sequence
items.content: A backslash followed by a character represents a special character sequence, such as newline or tab.

items.title: Common escape sequences
items.content: \\n = newline | \\t = tab | \\\\ = backslash | \\' = single quote | \\" = double quote

items.title: List
items.content: An ordered, mutable collection of elements enclosed in square brackets [].

items.title: Creating a list
items.content: L = [element1, element2, element3]

items.title: List indexing
items.content: Positive indexing starts at 0 from the left; negative indexing starts at -1 from the right.

items.title: List slicing
items.content: L[start:stop:step] extracts a portion of a list. The stop position is excluded.

items.title: Lists are mutable
items.content: Elements of an existing list can be changed using their index.

items.title: Changing a list element
items.content: L[index] = value

items.title: List concatenation
items.content: Use + to join two lists into a new list.

items.title: List repetition
items.content: Use * with an integer to repeat the elements of a list.

items.title: List membership
items.content: Use in or not in to test whether an element occurs in a list.

items.title: len() for lists
items.content: len(L) returns the number of elements in list L.

items.title: append()
items.content: L.append(x) adds x as a single element at the end of the list.

items.title: extend()
items.content: L.extend(iterable) adds each element of the iterable to the end of the list.

items.title: insert()
items.content: L.insert(index, x) inserts x before the specified index.

items.title: remove()
items.content: L.remove(x) removes the first occurrence of x from the list.

items.title: pop()
items.content: L.pop(index) removes and returns the element at index. With no index, the last element is removed.

items.title: index()
items.content: L.index(x) returns the index of the first occurrence of x.

items.title: count()
items.content: L.count(x) returns the number of occurrences of x in the list.

items.title: sort()
items.content: L.sort() rearranges the list in ascending order by default.

items.title: reverse()
items.content: L.reverse() reverses the order of elements in the list.

items.title: clear()
items.content: L.clear() removes all elements from the list.

items.title: copy()
items.content: L.copy() returns a shallow copy of the list.

items.title: Nested list
items.content: A list containing one or more lists as its elements.

items.title: List assignment and aliasing
items.content: If b = a, both variables refer to the same list object; changing the list through one reference affects the other.

items.title: List traversal
items.content: for element in L:\n    statement

items.title: Tuple
items.content: An ordered, immutable collection of elements, commonly written using parentheses ().

items.title: Creating a tuple
items.content: T = (element1, element2, element3)

items.title: Single-element tuple
items.content: T = (element,)

items.title: Tuple indexing
items.content: Positive indexing starts at 0 from the left; negative indexing starts at -1 from the right.

items.title: Tuple slicing
items.content: T[start:stop:step] extracts a portion of a tuple. The stop position is excluded.

items.title: Tuples are immutable
items.content: Elements of an existing tuple cannot be changed, added or removed directly.

items.title: Tuple concatenation
items.content: Use + to join two tuples into a new tuple.

items.title: Tuple repetition
items.content: Use * with an integer to repeat the elements of a tuple.

items.title: Tuple membership
items.content: Use in or not in to test whether an element occurs in a tuple.

items.title: len() for tuples
items.content: len(T) returns the number of elements in tuple T.

items.title: count()
items.content: T.count(x) returns the number of occurrences of x in the tuple.

items.title: index()
items.content: T.index(x) returns the index of the first occurrence of x.

items.title: Nested tuple
items.content: A tuple containing another tuple as one of its elements.

items.title: Tuple packing
items.content: Multiple values can be grouped into a tuple using comma-separated values.

items.title: Tuple unpacking
items.content: Elements of a tuple can be assigned to multiple variables in one statement.

items.title: Tuple without parentheses
items.content: Parentheses are optional in many tuple assignments; commas are what form the tuple.

items.title: Tuple traversal
items.content: for element in T:\n    statement

items.title: Dictionary
items.content: A mutable collection that stores data as key-value pairs, written using curly braces {}.

items.title: Creating a dictionary
items.content: D = {key1: value1, key2: value2}

items.title: Dictionary key
items.content: A key identifies a value in a dictionary. Keys must be unique and hashable.

items.title: Dictionary keys are unique
items.content: A dictionary cannot contain duplicate keys. Assigning a value to an existing key replaces its previous value.

items.title: Dictionaries are mutable
items.content: Dictionary entries can be added, changed or removed after creation.

items.title: Accessing a value
items.content: D[key]

items.title: Adding or updating an entry
items.content: D[key] = value

items.title: del statement
items.content: del D[key] removes the specified key-value pair.

items.title: Dictionary membership
items.content: in and not in test whether a key exists in the dictionary.

items.title: len() for dictionaries
items.content: len(D) returns the number of key-value pairs in dictionary D.

items.title: keys()
items.content: D.keys() returns a view containing the dictionary keys.

items.title: values()
items.content: D.values() returns a view containing the dictionary values.

items.title: items()
items.content: D.items() returns a view containing key-value pairs.

items.title: get()
items.content: D.get(key) returns the value associated with key, or None if the key is absent.

items.title: update()
items.content: D.update(other) adds or updates key-value pairs from another mapping or iterable of pairs.

items.title: pop()
items.content: D.pop(key) removes the specified key and returns its associated value.

items.title: clear()
items.content: D.clear() removes all key-value pairs from the dictionary.

items.title: copy()
items.content: D.copy() returns a shallow copy of the dictionary.

items.title: Nested dictionary
items.content: A dictionary containing another dictionary as a value.

items.title: Dictionary traversal
items.content: for key in D:\n    statement

items.title: Traversing key-value pairs
items.content: for key, value in D.items():\n    statement

items.title: Dictionary order
items.content: Dictionaries preserve insertion order in modern Python implementations.

items.title: KeyError
items.content: Accessing D[key] with a key that does not exist raises a KeyError.

items.title: Dictionary versus list
items.content: A list accesses elements by position, while a dictionary accesses values using keys.

items.title: Module
items.content: A Python file containing definitions and statements that can be imported and reused in another program.

items.title: Purpose of modules
items.content: Modules help organize programs and allow reusable code to be used across programs.

items.title: Import a module
items.content: import module_name

items.title: Import with alias
items.content: import module_name as alias

items.title: Import a specific member
items.content: from module_name import member_name

items.title: Import multiple members
items.content: from module_name import member1, member2

items.title: Using an imported member
items.content: After import module_name, access a member using module_name.member_name.

items.title: Common math module functions
items.content: The math module provides mathematical functions and constants such as sqrt(), ceil(), floor(), factorial() and pi.

items.title: Import math module
items.content: import math

items.title: math.sqrt()
items.content: math.sqrt(x) returns the square root of x.

items.title: math.ceil()
items.content: math.ceil(x) returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to x.

items.title: math.floor()
items.content: math.floor(x) returns the largest integer less than or equal to x.

items.title: math.factorial()
items.content: math.factorial(n) returns n factorial for a non-negative integer n.

items.title: math.pi
items.content: math.pi provides the mathematical constant pi.

items.title: Random module
items.content: import random

items.title: random.randint()
items.content: random.randint(a, b) returns a random integer N such that a <= N <= b.

items.title: random.randrange()
items.content: random.randrange(start, stop, step) returns a randomly selected value from the specified range; stop is excluded.

items.title: Standard library module
items.content: A module supplied as part of the Python standard library and available without installing an external package.

items.title: Module import rule
items.content: A module or member must be imported before using names provided by it, unless it is already available in the current namespace.

items.title: Digital Footprint
items.content: The trail of information and activities a person leaves behind while using digital devices and online services.

items.title: Active Digital Footprint
items.content: Data deliberately shared or created by a user, such as posts, comments, uploads and online forms.

items.title: Passive Digital Footprint
items.content: Data collected about a user without the user actively submitting it, such as browsing or usage information.

items.title: Digital footprint persistence
items.content: Information shared online can remain accessible or may be copied, archived or reshared even after the original content is removed.

items.title: Think before posting
items.content: Consider the audience, permanence and possible consequences before sharing information online.

items.title: Examples of digital footprints
items.content: Social media posts, comments, searches, website visits, uploaded files, online purchases and account activity can contribute to a digital footprint.

items.title: Digital footprint and privacy
items.content: A larger or poorly managed digital footprint can expose personal information and increase privacy risks.

items.title: Minimize unnecessary sharing
items.content: Share only information that is necessary and appropriate for the intended audience.

items.title: Online reputation
items.content: A person’s digital footprint can influence how others perceive them online.

items.title: Managing a digital footprint
items.content: Review privacy settings, remove unnecessary public information where possible and regularly check what information about you is visible online.

items.title: Cookies and digital traces
items.content: Websites may use cookies and similar technologies to store or collect information about browsing activity.

items.title: Protect personal information
items.content: Avoid unnecessarily publishing sensitive personal information such as passwords, authentication details or private contact information.

items.title: Digital footprint and future opportunities
items.content: Public online content may be encountered later by educational institutions, employers or other audiences.

items.title: Positive digital footprint
items.content: Responsible, respectful and useful online contributions can help build a positive digital presence.

items.title: Digital Society
items.content: A society in which digital technologies and online services play an important role in communication, education, work and everyday activities.

items.title: Netizen
items.content: A person who actively participates in the digital or online community.

items.title: Digital Citizenship
items.content: Responsible, safe, respectful and informed participation in the digital world.

items.title: Netiquette
items.content: The accepted rules of polite, respectful and responsible behaviour while communicating online.

items.title: Respectful online communication
items.content: Communicate politely and avoid abusive, threatening or discriminatory behaviour online.

items.title: Digital identity
items.content: The collection of information and online activities associated with a person in digital environments.

items.title: Digital inclusion
items.content: Ensuring that people can access and meaningfully use digital technologies and services.

items.title: Digital divide
items.content: The gap between people or communities that have effective access to digital technologies and those that do not.

items.title: Respect privacy online
items.content: Do not access, share or disclose another person’s private information without appropriate permission.

items.title: Intellectual property awareness
items.content: Digital citizens should respect ownership and legal rights associated with digital content, software and other creative works.

items.title: Avoid misinformation sharing
items.content: Check the reliability of information before forwarding or publishing it online.

items.title: Responsible digital participation
items.content: A responsible netizen considers the social, ethical, legal and privacy consequences of online actions.

items.title: Examples of digital society activities
items.content: Online learning, digital payments, e-governance, social networking, digital communication and online collaboration are examples of digital activities.

items.title: Respect accessibility and inclusion
items.content: Digital content and communication should consider the needs and accessibility of different users.

items.title: Online collaboration
items.content: Digital platforms allow users to communicate, share resources and work together across different locations.

items.title: Verify before trusting online information
items.content: Consider the source, evidence, date and context of online information before accepting or sharing it.

items.title: Cyber Safety
items.content: Practices used to protect digital devices, accounts, information and users from online risks.

items.title: Strong password
items.content: Use a long, unique password or passphrase for each important account and avoid easily guessed personal information.

items.title: Multi-factor authentication
items.content: An authentication method that requires more than one type of verification before access is granted.

items.title: Phishing
items.content: A social-engineering attack in which a person is deceived into revealing information or performing an unsafe action through a fraudulent message or website.

items.title: Social Engineering
items.content: Manipulating people into revealing information or taking actions that may compromise security.

items.title: Common phishing warning signs
items.content: Unexpected messages, urgent requests, suspicious links, unusual sender addresses and requests for sensitive information can indicate phishing.

items.title: Safe link practice
items.content: Check the destination and context of a link before opening it, especially when it arrives unexpectedly.

items.title: Safe download practice
items.content: Download software and files only from trusted sources and avoid suspicious or unexpected attachments.

items.title: Malware
items.content: Malicious software designed to disrupt, damage, misuse or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.

items.title: Keep software updated
items.content: Install security and software updates from trusted sources to reduce exposure to known vulnerabilities.

items.title: Use secure networks
items.content: Avoid entering sensitive information on untrusted or unsecured networks and prefer trusted protected connections.

items.title: Protect personal information
items.content: Do not unnecessarily disclose passwords, authentication codes, financial information or other sensitive personal data.

items.title: Backup important data
items.content: Maintain suitable backups of important files so that data can be recovered after accidental loss or certain security incidents.

items.title: Review privacy settings
items.content: Regularly review account and application privacy settings and limit unnecessary access to personal information.

items.title: Report suspicious activity
items.content: Report suspected cyber incidents, fraudulent messages or harmful online behaviour to an appropriate trusted authority or platform.

items.title: Cyber safety principle
items.content: Good cyber safety combines secure authentication, cautious online behaviour, privacy protection, software maintenance and data protection.

items.title: Cyber Crime
items.content: An unlawful activity in which a computer, digital device, network or online service is used as a target, tool or part of the offence.

items.title: Hacking
items.content: Unauthorized access to or interference with a computer system, account or network.

items.title: Identity Theft
items.content: Unauthorized use of another person’s identity or personal information for fraudulent or unlawful purposes.

items.title: Cyber Fraud
items.content: Fraudulent activity carried out using digital technologies, online services or electronic communication.

items.title: Phishing
items.content: A fraudulent attempt to obtain information or cause an unsafe action by pretending to be a trustworthy person or organization.

items.title: Cyberbullying
items.content: Using digital communication or online platforms to repeatedly harass, threaten, humiliate or harm another person.

items.title: Cyberstalking
items.content: Repeated unwanted monitoring, communication or harassment of a person through digital technologies.

items.title: Malware
items.content: Malicious software created to disrupt operations, damage systems, misuse resources or gain unauthorized access to data or devices.

items.title: Ransomware
items.content: A type of malware that prevents access to data or systems and is commonly associated with demands for payment.

items.title: Denial-of-Service Attack
items.content: An attack intended to make a computer service or network resource unavailable to legitimate users by overwhelming or disrupting it.

items.title: Data Theft
items.content: Unauthorized acquisition, copying or removal of digital information.

items.title: Cyber Defamation
items.content: Using digital communication to publish or spread false or harmful statements about a person or organization in a way that may cause reputational harm.

items.title: Cyber Crime Targets
items.content: Cyber crimes may target individuals, organizations, computer systems, networks, data or online services.

items.title: Do not participate in cyber crime
items.content: Unauthorized access, fraud, harassment, data theft and other unlawful digital activities can cause harm and may have legal consequences.

items.title: Preserve evidence of cyber incidents
items.content: When a cyber incident occurs, preserve relevant messages, notifications or other available evidence and report the incident through an appropriate channel.

items.title: Cyber crime prevention
items.content: Use strong authentication, protect personal information, keep software updated, verify suspicious communications and report suspected incidents.

items.title: Cyber Law
items.content: The legal framework that governs activities involving computers, digital systems, networks, electronic records and online communication.

items.title: Information Technology Act, 2000
items.content: The Information Technology Act, 2000 provides an important legal framework in India for electronic records, electronic communication and specified cyber-related offences.

items.title: Electronic Record
items.content: Information created, stored, received or transmitted in electronic form can have legal significance under applicable law.

items.title: Electronic Signature
items.content: An electronic method used to authenticate or sign an electronic record according to applicable legal requirements.

items.title: Cyber Offence
items.content: An unlawful act involving a computer resource, communication device, network, digital information or online service.

items.title: Unauthorized access is unlawful
items.content: Accessing computer resources or accounts without authorization can constitute an offence under applicable law.

items.title: Data Protection and Privacy
items.content: Responsible digital use includes protecting personal information and respecting applicable privacy and data-protection requirements.

items.title: Copyright
items.content: A legal protection granted to creators for eligible original creative works, subject to applicable law and limitations.

items.title: Software Copyright
items.content: Computer programs can be protected as intellectual property, and unauthorized copying or distribution may violate applicable rights.

items.title: Plagiarism
items.content: Presenting another person’s work, ideas or expression as one’s own without appropriate acknowledgment.

items.title: Intellectual Property Rights
items.content: Legal rights that protect eligible creations such as literary works, software, inventions, designs and other intellectual creations.

items.title: Respect intellectual property
items.content: Use digital content, software and other intellectual creations according to applicable permissions, licences and laws.

items.title: Cyber Law and Responsible Use
items.content: Cyber laws establish legal boundaries for activities involving digital systems and help address misuse of technology.

items.title: Cyber law awareness
items.content: Users should understand that online actions can have legal as well as social and ethical consequences.

items.title: Legal and Ethical Difference
items.content: An action can involve both legal and ethical considerations; legality concerns applicable law, while ethics concerns principles of responsible behaviour.

items.title: Use digital resources lawfully
items.content: Do not misuse computer resources, infringe intellectual property rights or perform unauthorized digital activities.

items.title: Computer Ethics
items.content: Principles and standards that guide responsible, fair and appropriate use of computers and digital technologies.

items.title: Privacy
items.content: The right and expectation that personal information should be handled appropriately and protected from unjustified access or disclosure.

items.title: Intellectual Property
items.content: Legal and ethical rights associated with creations such as software, written works, images, music and other intellectual creations.

items.title: Plagiarism
items.content: Using another person’s work, ideas or expression without appropriate acknowledgment and presenting it as one’s own.

items.title: Software Piracy
items.content: Unauthorized copying, distribution or use of software in violation of applicable licensing or intellectual property rights.

items.title: Digital Divide
items.content: The unequal access to digital technologies, connectivity, skills or opportunities among different people or communities.

items.title: Accessibility
items.content: Designing digital technologies and content so that people with different abilities can access and use them effectively.

items.title: Cyberbullying and Ethics
items.content: Using digital platforms to harm, humiliate, threaten or repeatedly harass others raises serious ethical and social concerns.

items.title: Respect others online
items.content: Communicate responsibly and avoid harassment, abuse, discrimination and deliberate harm in digital spaces.

items.title: Responsible Disclosure
items.content: Security weaknesses should be reported responsibly to the appropriate organization or authority rather than being misused.

items.title: Open Source Software
items.content: Software whose source code is made available under a licence that permits specified use, modification or redistribution according to its terms.

items.title: Respect software licences
items.content: Use, copy, modify and distribute software according to the conditions of its applicable licence.

items.title: Academic Integrity
items.content: Being honest and responsible in academic work, including properly acknowledging sources and submitting original work.

items.title: Digital Accessibility and Inclusion
items.content: Ethical digital design should aim to reduce barriers and allow diverse users to participate meaningfully.

items.title: Verify information before sharing
items.content: Avoid knowingly spreading false or misleading information and consider the possible effects of sharing unverified content.

items.title: Core principles of computer ethics
items.content: Respect privacy, intellectual property, security, accessibility, academic integrity and the rights of other users.

items.title: Ethical decision-making online
items.content: Before taking a digital action, consider its effect on others, respect for rights and privacy, applicable rules and the possibility of harm.
